lots.title: 1963 Chevrolet Corvette Sting Ray
lots.alt: White 1963 Chevrolet Corvette Sting Ray convertible
lots.lead: A Corvette with the single most debated design in its history
text: The 1963 Sting Ray introduced independent rear suspension and the sharp lines of Larry Shinoda's design to the Corvette. This example has the 327 V8 and a four-speed manual, both numbers-matching.
It has been in the same family collection since 1991 and was repainted in its original colour. The interior is the correct red vinyl with period-correct gauges and a Wonderbar radio.
lots.history: Delivered new through a Chevrolet dealer in Tulsa, imported to Australia in 1991 and kept by one family since.
lots.quote: A design that has not dated in sixty years.

lots.title: 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing
lots.alt: Red 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing with its doors raised
lots.lead: The first production car with fuel injection, with doors that open like wings
text: The 300 SL's tubular space frame forced the designers to raise the door sills, and the gullwing doors were the answer. This car retains its original fitted luggage, a feature of the first cars.
Fully documented with a Mercedes-Benz Classic certificate and a long record of specialist care.
lots.history: Sold new in Germany, exported in the 1960s and repatriated in 2011 for a full restoration.
lots.quote: One of the most desirable cars ever built.

lots.title: 1964 Jaguar E-Type Series 1
lots.alt: Blue 1964 Jaguar E-Type Series 1 coupe in profile
lots.lead: Enzo Ferrari called it the most beautiful car ever made
text: A Series 1 coupe with the 3.8-litre engine and the early all-synchromesh gearbox. It wears its original colour with wire wheels and the slim-bumper body.
One family owner for decades, with a complete file including the original buff logbook.
lots.history: Built in Coventry in 1964, sold through a London dealer and kept by one family from 1982.
lots.quote: A shape that has never needed improving.

lots.title: 1972 Porsche 911 S Targa
lots.alt: Cream 1972 Porsche 911 Targa on a country road
lots.lead: The last of the long-hood 911s before the impact bumpers
text: The 2.4-litre S was the quickest and most refined of the early 911s. This Targa has matching numbers and has been driven on rallies.
The Targa roof and removable rear window give open-air motoring with the structure of a coupe.
lots.history: Delivered new in Stuttgart and has competed in classic rallies across Europe.
lots.quote: A car that rewards being driven.

lots.title: 1967 Chevrolet Camaro SS 350
lots.alt: Black 1967 Chevrolet Camaro SS convertible with white stripes
lots.lead: Black paint and white stripes on a first-generation Camaro
text: The 1967 SS convertible in Tuxedo Black with white stripes and a black top. The 350 V8 was rebuilt in 2018.
Chrome and trim have been restored and the interior is largely original.
lots.history: A US-market car that moved to Germany in 2004 and has been on club tours ever since.
lots.quote: American muscle with a clean sheet of paper.

lots.title: 1967 Shelby GT500 KR
lots.lead: King of the Road, in period black
text: The KR stands for King of the Road. This fastback has the 428 Cobra Jet engine and the Shelby-specific fibreglass hood.
It has a complete file and has been shown at several European concours.
lots.history: Built in California in 1967, sold through a Shelby dealer and imported to Germany in 1998.
lots.quote: A fixture of the sale for its condition and file.

lots.title: 1970 Dodge Challenger R/T
lots.alt: Lime green 1970 Dodge Challenger R/T with a black hood stripe
lots.lead: Sublime Green with a Hemi, a combination that built a legend
text: The 426 Hemi was a race engine sold for the street. This R/T has a black hood stripe and the original shaker scoop.
Restored with a documented build and a Dodge broadcast sheet.
lots.history: Sold new in Detroit, restored in 2015 and exported to Australia in 2020.
lots.quote: No reserve. Whoever bids highest owns it.

lots.title: 1969 Ford Mustang Boss 429
lots.alt: Red 1969 Ford Mustang Boss 429 with its hood raised
lots.lead: Built so Ford could homologate the engine for NASCAR
text: Only 859 Boss 429 Mustangs were built in 1969. The engine barely fits, and the car was finished by Kar Kraft in Michigan.
This example is Candy Apple Red, a colour used on a small number of cars.
lots.history: Kar Kraft built, delivered through a Charlotte dealer and in single-family ownership until 2012.
lots.quote: A homologation special that became a collector's grail.

lots.title: 1951 Pontiac Chieftain
text: The Chieftain's silver-streak trim and straight-eight engine make it distinctive. This convertible has a power top and original hubcaps.
It has spent most of its life in a warm climate and shows little corrosion.
lots.history: A Florida car since new, kept in a collection from 1994.
lots.quote: Chrome, colour and a big flathead.

lots.title: 1969 Excalibur Roadster
lots.lead: A neo-classic with a 1920s silhouette and a Corvette engine
text: Brooks Stevens built the Excalibur as a modern take on the Mercedes SSK. This roadster has the side-mounted exhausts and a Corvette 327.
The body and brightwork are in excellent order.
lots.history: Bought new in Milwaukee and sold to its second owner in 1998.

lots.title: 1965 Ford Mustang Coupe
lots.lead: The car that started the pony-car era
text: A 1965 coupe in Poppy Red with a 289 V8 and a manual gearbox. Fitted with Magnum 500 wheels.
Right-hand drive, converted in period for the UK.
lots.history: Imported to the UK in 1966, in the same hands for over twenty years.
lots.quote: The simplest way into an American classic.

lots.title: 1963 Chevrolet Impala SS
lots.lead: Low, black and lit by amber headlights
text: A 1963 Impala SS with a 409 V8 and a four-speed, lowered on wire wheels in the West Coast style.
The black paint is deep and the chrome is clean.
lots.history: A California car since new and the subject of a full cosmetic restoration.
